title: Generation of Transgenic Rats using a Lentiviral Vector Approach
protocol: Culture HEK 293T cells in DMEM medium supplemented with fetal bovine serum (10%, v/v) in a humidified CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Seed 1.5–2 x 10^6 HEK 293T cells per Ø10 cm culture dish when confluence reaches ~70% for transfection.
Transfect the cells using polyethylenimine (PEI) reagent, pH 7.0, at a ratio of 3 μg of PEI per 1 μg of DNA.
Prepare the transfection mixture with 25 µg of VSVg plasmid, 50 µg of delta R8.2, and 50 µg of coding plasmid for five plates.
Pipette up and down, and add 125 µL of PEI at a concentration of 3 µg/µL.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min, inverting the tube three times during incubation.
Add 200 µL of the transfection mixture per plate.
Incubate the plates in a humidified CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Harvest the medium containing LV particles forty-eight hours after transfection using 50 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge the medium at 3,000 x g for 5 min and room temperature to remove detached cells.
Filter the supernatant (0.45 µm) and pour it into new tubes.
Add DNase I (RNase-free, 1 μg/mL) and MgCl2 (1 mM), and incubate in a water bath at 37 °C for 15 min.
Transfer the medium to disposable polyethylene tubes.
Ultracentrifuge in a swinging rotor at 115,000 x g and 4 °C for 1.5 h.
Gently drain the walls of the tubes from the medium residues after centrifuging.
Soak the pellet with sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS; 70–80 µL per tube).
Incubate for 2 h at 4–8 °C.
Resuspend the viral vectors in PBS by gentle pipetting.
Transfer the solution to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 7,000 x g and 4 °C for 30 seconds.
Remove and transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Repeat the centrifugation step until no cellular debris is visible.
Aliquot the supernatant and store at -80 °C.
Avoid refreezing the LV aliquot.
Prepare serial dilutions of the LV-coding plasmid: 1:500, 1:1,000, 1:5,000, 1:10,000, 1:100,000, and 1:1,000,000.
Determine the number of copies per µL using Avogadro's number and plasmid size.
Prepare dilutions of lentiviral suspension: 1:100, 1:500, and 1:1,000.
Mix 10 µL qPCR Mastermix, 1 µL forward primer (10 μM), 1 µL reverse primer (10 μM), and 7 µL H2O for each reaction well.
Pipette the mixture into wells of a 96-well plate.
Add 1 µL of each standard dilution in triplicate to the appropriate wells.
Add 1 µL of each lentiviral suspension dilution in triplicate to other designated wells.
Run the qPCR according to the following parameters.
Set temperature to 50 °C for 2 minutes.
Increase temperature to 96 °C for 5 minutes.
Cycle through 35 cycles of 96 °C for 20 seconds, 60 °C for 40 seconds, and 70 °C for 1 minute.
Perform melt curve analysis: increase temperature to 95 °C for 1 minute followed by 60 °C at 30 seconds.
Analyze the results by comparing the number of molecules received for each dilution to the standard curve.
Determine the concentration of vector molecules as the average of three replicates for each dilution.
Administer gonadotropins according to protocol.
Prepare pregnant mare’s serum gonadotropin (PMSG) working solution at a concentration of 125 IU/mL by dissolving hormone powder in 0.9% NaCl.
Store PMSG working solution in 1 mL aliquots at -20 °C for up to 1 month or -80 °C for up to 6 months.
Inject immature 5-week-old Wistar females with PMSG (25 IU per female) intraperitoneally on Day 1 between 12 PM and 1 PM.
Prepare human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) working solution at a concentration of 150 IU/mL by dissolving hormone powder in 0.9% NaCl.
Store hCG working solution in 1 mL aliquots at -20 °C for up to 1 month or -80 °C for up to 6 months.
Inject immature 5-week-old Wistar females with hCG (30 IU per female) intraperitoneally on Day 3 between 12 PM and 1 PM.
Mate females 1:1 with sexually fertile males after hCG administration.
Check females for the presence of a vaginal plug in the morning (day 4 between 8–10 AM).
Collect embryos from females with a visible whitish mating plug at 10 AM.
Sacrifice animals to excise oviducts.
Collect oviducts in a dish containing pre-warmed M2 medium.
Transfer oviducts to a 35 mm dish with pre-warmed M2 medium and hyaluronidase from bovine testes (0.5 mg/mL).
Open the walls of the oviduct using fine forceps under a stereomicroscope.
Press the ampulla until fertilized embryos are freed.
Gently pipette up and down to release embryos from cumulus cells using a glass transfer pipette connected to a mouth-operated aspirator tube.
Pull a glass Pasteur pipette over a flame to produce a straight tip of ~5-10 cm.
Break the pipette leaving a ~4 cm tip.
Wash embryos in M2 medium to remove hyaluronidase and cellular debris.
Transfer embryos to a 60 mm dish containing drops of pre-equilibrated M16 medium covered by liquid paraffin or mineral oil.
Place the dish in a humidified 37 °C incubator with a 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Select one-cell-stage embryos with two visible pronuclei for microinjection.
Thaw the LV aliquot at room temperature.
Centrifuge the thawed LV aliquot at 10,000 x g and room temperature for 2 minutes to pellet cellular debris.
Prepare glass holding pipettes using a microforge by pulling borosilicate glass capillary over a flame.
Break the prepared pipette leaving a ~4 cm tip with an outside diameter of ~80–120 µm.
Ensure that the pipette tip is perfectly straight and smooth.
Assemble the pulled pipette in a microforge with the tip in front of the heating filament.
Heat the filament very close to the pipette tip and allow it to shrink to a diameter of ~15 µm (approximately 20% of embryo size).
Position the pipette perpendicularly to the heating filament, 2–3 mm from the pipette tip, and begin to heat.
Heat until it reaches a 15° angle.
Prepare microinjection borosilicate glass capillaries with a filament using a pipette puller.
Insert the capillary in the pulling chamber.
Run a ramp test (for the first time for new glass and every time after changing the filament).
Set the Heat to the ramp value -10, Pull to 100, Velocity to 150 and Time to 100.
Modify the parameters to obtain an optimal injection capillary.
Under a biosafety laminar flow hood, load approximately 2 µL of the viral solution into the microinjection pipette with a microloader tip.
Prepare a microinjection dish (lid of 60 mm Petri dish) with a 100 µL drop of M2 medium (in the middle), covered by liquid paraffin or mineral oil.
Mount the holding pipette and microinjection capillary that is loaded with viral solution to a micromanipulator and microinjection dish under an inverted microscope.
Transfer 15–20 one-cell-stage embryos to the M2 drop on the microinjection dish.
Hold the embryo using a holding pipette.
Inject the LV solution under the zona pellucida to the perivitelline space using a glass capillary connected to an automatic injector.
Hold the capillary under the zona pellucida for a moment.
Return the embryos to the culture dish in the incubator at 37°C in a 5% CO2 atmosphere.

Prepare foster mothers by mating sexually mature SD females with fertile BN males or vasectomized SD males on day 3 (for transferring embryos at the one-cell stage) or day 4 (for transferring embryos at the two-cell stage).
Check SD females for a vaginal plug and use only those with a visible plug.
Conduct the surgical procedure with sterile instruments under a stereomicroscope.
Autoclave scissors, fine forceps, needle holder, and scalpel holder before surgery.
Anesthetize a female animal with i.p. administration of ketamine (50 mg/kg) and medetomidine (0.5 mg/kg).
Test for reflexes to confirm anesthesia before starting the surgical procedure.
Inject the animal subcutaneously with tolefenamic acid (2 mg/kg), butorphanol tartrate (1 mg/kg), and enrofloksacin (5–10 mg/kg).
Apply ophthalmic ointment lubrication to both eyes to prevent corneal drying.
Shave the fur from the back of the animal.
Sterilize the skin with surgical scrub followed by 70% alcohol using sterile non-adhering pads.
Allow the skin to dry completely.
Inject the animal subcutaneously with 100 µL of 0.25% bupivacaine at the incision site.
Transfer the animal in a prone position to a clean surface on a heating pad under the objective of a surgical microscope.
Cover the rat with a sterile drape with a small hole cut over the lower back.
Perform an approximately 2 cm skin incision, parallel to the lumbar vertebral column.
Using sharp scissors, make a cut in the abdominal wall.
Grab an ovarian fat pad using forceps.
Pull out the ovary and oviduct and place them on gauze that is wetted with 0.9% NaCl.
Aspirate M2 medium, three bubbles of air, and the embryos into the transfer capillary.
Make a small incision in the oviduct (between the infundibulum and ampulla) using micro-scissors.
Insert the transfer pipette into the oviduct.
Gently expel embryos and air bubbles from the pipette to the oviduct.
Place the reproductive tract back in the abdominal cavity with blunt forceps.
Suture the abdominal wall with polyglycolic acid absorbable sutures.
Close the skin incision with wound clips.
Inject the animal intraperitoneally with atipamezole (0.5 mg/kg) to reverse the effect of anesthesia.
Transfer the animal to a clean cage and keep it on a warming plate to fully recover from anesthesia.
Anesthetize a 5-week-old male SD rat with i.p. administration of ketamine (50 mg/kg) and medetomidine (0.5 mg/kg).
Test for reflexes to confirm anesthesia before starting the surgical procedure.
Administer tolfenamic acid (2 mg/kg), butorphanol tartrate (1 mg/kg), and enrofloksacin (5–10 mg/kg) subcutaneously.
Apply ophthalmic ointment lubrication to both eyes.
Place the rat supine on a clean surface on a heating pad.
Sterilize the skin on the testes with surgical scrub followed by 70% alcohol using sterile non-adhering pads.
Allow the skin to dry.
Cover the rat with a sterile drape with a small hole cut over the testes.
Gently press the abdomen to expose the testes in the scrotal sac.
Make a ~0.5 cm incision in the middle of the scrotal sac.
Locate the midline wall (whitish line) between the testes.
Make a 5 mm incision in the testis membrane close to the left side of the midline wall.
Carefully push the testis to the left and locate vas deferens as a white duct with a single blood vessel.
Gently pull the vas deferens out of the scrotal sac using a watchmaker’s forceps.
Hold the vas deferns with one pair of forceps, and cut it with fine scissors or cauterize with red-hot tips of a second pair of forceps.
Remove a ~1 cm fragment of the duct.
